payload.title: The production droplet disk is 91% used (21.5 GiB free of 227 GiB), so a full deploy cannot pass its capacity gate and the gate floors were lowered to leave about 4.5 GiB free after the worst-case image pull
evidence: scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh:67 (full-deploy byte floor lowered from 35 to 20 GiB)
scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh:79 (full-deploy percent floor lowered from 10 to 5)
scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh:88 (full pull estimate measured at 17 GiB: 16 backend images of ~1.0 GB unique layers plus web)
scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh:93 (projected reserve lowered from 20 to 3 GiB)
payload.rule_violated: The deploy capacity gate keeps headroom for the pull and for the data volumes on the same filesystem (ADR 033 pull-only runtime)
payload.notes: Owner decision (Okan, 2026-10-28): lower the floors. Not done: the disk is not enlarged and the stale-deploy refusal is untouched. Postgres, Redis and NATS volumes share the filesystem, so a pull that overruns the estimate fills the disk under production. Enlarge the DigitalOcean disk or move images to a volume.
